thread:
incident-bot: PAGE — Sev2: streaming route SLO breach detected. streaming.p99 > 3s for 6m (route=/v1/stream, pool=shared-gpu-pool-3). Paging @laura (oncall). Runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail
laura (oncall): ack, I'm on it. quick snapshot: p95 ~820ms, p99 ~3.8s, tail outliers hitting 8-12s for some streaming chunks. Errors: a bunch of `stream stall` traces and `kv_cache_miss` floods. :eyes:
mike (eng-runtime): seeing continuous KV cache churn for tenant_id=acme-42. large seq lengths, repeated full-cache fills -> heavy GPU mem churn + stalled dispatches. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T13:21:02Z] tenant=acme-42 seq_len=32768 kv_evictions=1245 stall=1
[2026-03-15T13:21:04Z] dispatch_delay=120ms gpu_queue_wait=980ms
```
mike (eng-runtime): also seeing host nvme write latency spikes on host gpu-node-17: iowait and blkio stats look bad. this looks multi-tenant IO/cgroup related.
priya (eng-infra): confirmed iostat on gpu-node-17: avg await ~95ms, util 99%. blkio service bytes shows sustained write bursts. cgroup weights for some containers are very low -> noisy neighbor risk.
laura (oncall): immediate mitigations in flight:
  - pause streaming batching for pool shared-gpu-pool-3 (quick toggle) to reduce IO fanout
  - soft-evacuate hot pod gpu-pod-17a (cordon -> move 2 biggest tenants to spare hosts)
  - apply temporary per-tenant write_iops cap for tenant acme-42
commands I ran:
```
# pause batching
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.local/configs -d '{"pool":"shared-gpu-pool-3","streaming_batching":false}'
# drain pod
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
priya (eng-infra): applied temp blkio throttle: 
```
echo 1048576 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
priya (eng-infra): also bumped cgroup weight for streaming containers to reduce unfair scheduling.
maya (cust-success): FYI I reached out to acme-corp support contact (Alex) and told them we're investigating and will notify when mitigated. they reported saw stalls starting at 13:22 UTC and customer impact on live demo.
laura (oncall): initial results: after pausing batching + soft-evac, p99 dropped to ~1.1s within 3 mins, p95 ~420ms. still above target but improving. marking mitigation=true in incident tracker: https://go/redwood/incidents/3895000123
mike (eng-runtime): follow-up plan:
  - implement hot-tenant detector (prefix-length + sustained KV evictions) to auto-soft-evacuate
  - add per-tenant streaming batch limiter in runtime (prevent one tenant from forcing big IO bursts)
  - investigate KV cache eviction policy for long sequence workloads
laura (oncall): customer impact note: ACME (paid-dedicated) experienced degraded streaming UX for ~8m window, some dropped frames. Notifying sales/CS to offer credits if needed. :exclamation:
sarah (oncall-morning): acked — I'll take the postmortem and follow up first thing. please add all logs/metrics snapshots to the ticket. I'll run host-level fio tests later to validate recovery plan.
priya (eng-infra): opened infra follow-up ticket for QoS automation and host rebalancing: INFRA-2231
mike (eng-runtime): tagging runtime follow-ups: RUNTIME-1498 (hot-tenant detection), RUNTIME-1499 (per-tenant batch limiter)
laura (oncall): handoff: leaving notes in incident doc, key points: root likely multi-tenant IO pressure from large-seq tenant causing KV churn -> GPU stalls -> streaming tail latency. mitigations applied: pause batching, soft-evac, per-tenant io cap. monitor for 1 hour, escalate if p99 > 2s. handing to @sarah. :thumbsup:
sarah (oncall-morning): thanks — I'll monitor the dashboards and coordinate a scheduled re-run of the host once load subsides. please add any customer follow-up messages here and link support ticket.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity lowered to Sev3. Next update scheduled in 30m unless new pages.
